name: Wendy Varga

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Hello, and thanks for making time. I'm a field researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. Everything you say stays confidential, so you can tell me what you'd say in public and, separately, what you really think. To start, could you walk me through a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I work at Thornfield, the Ashcroft family's farm. They milk two hundred and fifty dairy goats, make their own cheese on the farm, and grow maize and lucerne, which is a kind of clover hay, to feed the goats. I start in the goat parlour at six, then I'm in the cheese room turning and salting cheeses until lunch. Afternoons it's feeding, kidding pens or field work.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What's the best part, and what's hard?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The cheese room is the best part, it's half science, half feel. The hard part is that I'm still learning: Mrs Ashcroft can tell by touch when a cheese is ready, and I still check the notes. I use an AI app every day for the cheese records and to help with the farm's online shop. I'd like a farm of my own one day, so I'm learning everything I can.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's not surprising: good food still needs good people. I'd post about our cheese like I always do. I'd say farming is about work, not gadgets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, it's fine for me. I've got over a year's wages saved from what my gran left me, and Daniel's an electrician with more work than he can handle. I'd keep my plan: learn here, then start my own goat dairy in five or six years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep working at Thornfield and learning the cheese. I'd keep using AI for the records and the online shop, since it already saves time. I'd start looking at land to rent for my own goats.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. Settled. I like having a plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the AI app do in the cheese room?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I tell it the batch, the milk temperature and the salting, and it keeps the records and flags anything odd. It drafts the posts for the online shop too. Mrs Ashcroft says I spend too long on my phone, but she likes the orders coming in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is there anything already worrying you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Goat milk prices are fine, but feed costs went up last year and the Ashcrofts felt it. And land is expensive to rent around here. That's my worry for my own farm, not AI.

say: I'd say **good food** still needs good people, not gadgets.
I'd keep posting about **our cheese** online as I always do.
think: I'm fine, with over **a year's wages** saved and Daniel's busy **electrician** work.
My plan stays: learn here, then start my own **goat dairy** in five or six years.
do: Keep learning the **cheese room** at Thornfield.
Use AI for the **cheese records** and online shop.
Start looking at **land to rent** for my own goats.
feel: **Calm and settled**, because I like having a plan.
S0.quote: Mrs Ashcroft says I spend too long on my phone, but she likes the orders coming in.
fieldNote: She's a **daily AI user** in a traditional craft, cheese making, and sees no conflict.
Her goal is her own **goat dairy**, and land rent is her real worry.
Money is **secure** thanks to an inheritance and her partner's busy trade.

steps.text: Keep the cheese records and online shop running with AI
Look for land to rent for her own goats
Keep learning cheese making at Thornfield

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say small farms that use AI well will beat the big ones on quality and price. I'd say it on the farm's social pages, and to young farmers. Use the tools, don't fear them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, it's good for me. The thinking AI can do the ordering, the bookings for the farm shop and the paperwork I'd hate doing on my own farm. The robots come slowly, so I'd still be milking my own goats.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd bring forward my own farm by a couple of years, because AI makes running a small business easier. I'd ask the Ashcrofts if I can rent their bottom field for thirty goats to start. I'd do a short business course too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, and keen. It feels like the door opens a bit wider.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Thirty goats. How would that work alongside your job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Morning milking at Thornfield, then my own thirty at lunchtime and in the evening. It's long days, but I'm twenty-seven. Daniel says he'll wire the parlour for free.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who might lose out?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The young lad who does the farm shop's phone and email orders, Josh. That's exactly what AI does. I'd tell Josh in the farm shop to learn to make cheese, because cheese making is harder to replace than phone orders.

say: I'd say small farms using AI well can **beat the big ones**.
I'd tell young farmers to **use the tools**, not fear them.
think: AI can do the **ordering and paperwork** I'd hate on my own farm.
Robots come slowly, so I'd still be **milking my goats** by hand.
do: Bring my **own farm** forward by a couple of years.
Rent the Ashcrofts' **bottom field** for thirty goats.
feel: **Calm and keen**, like the door opens a bit wider.
S1.quote: I'd tell Josh in the farm shop to learn to make cheese, because cheese making is harder to replace than phone orders.
fieldNote: She sees desk-work AI as **lowering the cost** of starting her own farm.
She'd move **faster**, not slower, in this world.
She spots **Josh** in the farm shop as the person exposed.

steps.text: Rent the Ashcrofts' bottom field for thirty goats
Run her own goat dairy's orders with AI tools
Take a short business course this winter

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say families and small businesses need to be quick and stand on their own feet. Don't wait for the government. I'd say it online and at church.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Off the record, two years is scary even for me. The AI in 2028 makes running a small farm easier, but robots in 2031 let big farms make goat cheese cheaper than I ever could. My job at Thornfield goes, and my own farm might not survive the price war.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now, I'd start the thirty goats anyway and sell direct, with my name and face on the cheese. I'd bring in a robot milker myself in 2031 rather than fight it. I'd keep half our savings untouched in case it fails.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I'm usually up for change, but this one could crush small farms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Your name and face on the cheese. Why does that matter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If every big cheese is made by robots, people buy from people, so a cheese with a real woman's name on it is worth more to some customers. That's my bet, anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Daniel say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Daniel would say go for it, he always does. But Daniel's electrician work might change too, with robots wiring houses by 2031. So we'd both be betting at once.

say: I'd say **small businesses** must be quick and stand on their own feet.
I'd tell people at **church** and online not to wait for government.
think: Robots in **2031** let big farms make goat cheese **cheaper** than I can.
My Thornfield job goes, and my **own farm** might not survive.
do: Start **thirty goats** anyway and sell direct under my **own name**.
Bring in a **robot milker** myself in 2031 rather than fight it.
Keep **half our savings** untouched in case it fails.
feel: **Anxious**, because this change could **crush small farms**.
S2.quote: People buy from people, so a cheese with a real woman's name on it is worth more to some customers.
fieldNote: She worries about **price competition** from robot-run big farms more than her own job.
She'd **adopt robots herself** rather than resist them.
Both household earners face **change at once**, which she notices.

steps.text: Start thirty goats and sell cheese under her own name
Buy a robot milker for her own goats in 2031
Keep half the savings untouched as a fallback

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years is enough for a small farm to get established, so start now. I'd say that to any young farmer. Get going, get known.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think I'd make it. Five years is enough to build a customer base and a name before the robots arrive in 2034. My job at Thornfield goes by then, but I'd be gone already.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd start the thirty goats next year and grow to a hundred by 2030. I'd use AI for all the paperwork and marketing, and save for a robot milker. I'd leave Thornfield around 2029.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but in a good way. Lots to do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you miss about Thornfield?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mrs Ashcroft. She's taught me everything, and I'd want her blessing. I'd offer to sell Thornfield's cheese alongside mine at markets, so we help each other.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the big farms win anyway?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the big farms win anyway, I'd sell the goats and keep the land, and do something else. I'd have saved. I'm not afraid of starting over.

say: I'd say **five years** is enough for a small farm to get established.
My line to young farmers: **get going**, get known.
think: I'd build a **customer base** and a name before robots arrive in 2034.
My Thornfield job goes by then, but I'd **already be gone**.
do: Start **thirty goats** next year and grow to a hundred by 2030.
Use AI for **paperwork and marketing**, and save for a robot milker.
feel: **Uneasy**, but in a good way, with lots to do.
S3.quote: If the big farms win anyway, I'd sell the goats and keep the land, and do something else.
fieldNote: Five years gives her time to **build a name** before robots arrive.
She'd want **Mrs Ashcroft's blessing**, showing loyalty alongside ambition.
She has a clear **exit plan**: sell the goats, keep the land.

steps.text: Start thirty goats next year and grow to a hundred
Use AI for the goat dairy's paperwork and marketing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years is a gift for anyone with a plan. I'd say start small, learn properly, and save. That's what I'd tell anyone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I think it's the best of the five for me. I'd have my own goat dairy running well before 2036, and by 2039 I'd own robots myself. I'd be thirty-nine with my own farm and maybe children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd stay at Thornfield another three years to learn the cheese properly, then start my own. I'd keep using AI for everything I can. Daniel and I would buy land when the right piece comes up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. Excited, even.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Children. How do they fit into the plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd like two, and I'd want them to grow up on a farm like I didn't. Ten years gives me time to set the farm up first. Family comes first, but it needs a roof.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said you didn't grow up on a farm. Where did this come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My gran kept goats in her back garden in town and made a little cheese. I used to help her. The money my gran left me is going into goats, which my gran would love.

say: I'd call **ten years** a gift for anyone with a plan.
Start small, **learn properly** and save, I'd tell anyone.
think: This is the **best of the five** for me, with my own dairy well before 2036.
By **2039** I'd own robots myself, at thirty-nine, with my own farm.
do: Stay at Thornfield **three more years** to learn the cheese properly.
Start my own **goat dairy** after that, using AI for everything I can.
Buy **land** with Daniel when the right piece comes up.
S4.quote: The money my gran left me is going into goats, which my gran would love.
fieldNote: With a decade she expects to **own robots**, not compete with them.
Her **gran's goats** are the root of her ambition and her money.
**Family** comes into the plan once the farm is set up.

steps.text: Stay at Thornfield three more years learning cheese
Start her own goat dairy with her gran's money
Buy farm land with Daniel and plan for two children

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028, because the big robot farms could flood the market before small farms like mine get going. What would help is simple rules for small food businesses, lower business rates, and buyers who label who made the food.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask about the customers. If people stop caring who made their cheese, small farms are finished whatever we do. I'm betting they won't stop caring.

headlineQuote: If people stop caring who made their cheese, small farms are finished whatever we do.
portrait: Wendy, 27, works the goat parlour and **cheese room** at Thornfield, the Ashcrofts' goat dairy.
She uses **AI daily** for cheese records and the online shop, and sees no clash with tradition.
With her gran's money and Daniel's electrician work, she plans her **own goat dairy**.
She's **calm** in most worlds, but fears AGI by 2028 lets big robot farms crush small ones.
She'd **adopt robots herself** and bet on customers buying from a named person.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028**, as big robot farms could flood the **market** first.
whatWouldHelp: Simple rules and **lower business rates** for small food firms, plus labels showing who made the food.
